size.note: Shoulder height, head-and-body length and tail length follow the ranges compiled on Wikipedia (citing Huffman, Ultimate Ungulate). Sexed mass follows Wikipedia (citing Kingdon 2015). Animal Diversity Web gives an unsexed mass of 118–270 kg and an average length of 123 cm, which sits inside the shoulder-height range. Male horns may reach 83 cm and female horns 30–40 cm (same Wikipedia compilation). No sexed shoulder-height split was found.

summary: A large, front-heavy antelope of open grassland. Adults are slate to bluish-grey with a black face, a black beard, a stiff black mane, and dark vertical brindle stripes on the neck and shoulders. Both sexes carry cow-like horns that spread out, then curve up and in. Calves are born tawny brown and stay close to the cow. Kruger holds a resident population; some local movement occurs inside the park, but this is not the long-distance East African migration.
description: The blue wildebeest is broad-shouldered, with a deep muzzle and high forequarters that slope down to the hips. Adult colour runs from deep slate or bluish-grey to lighter grey or greyish-brown, and the back and flanks are a little lighter than the underparts. Dark brown vertical stripes mark the neck and the side of the ribcage. The mane, face, beard and long tail are jet black in the southern subspecies, which is the form in Kruger. Males are larger and darker than females, and their horns are longer and heavier. The black wildebeest (Connochaetes gnou) does not occur in Kruger.
habits: Mostly active in the morning and late afternoon, and often rests in the heat of the day. Animals move in loose herds, from small groups to gatherings of many dozens, and commonly graze alongside Burchell's zebra. Territorial bulls mark ground with dung and scent, and they grunt, paw and horn the soil when challenging rivals. They can run at high speed when alarmed. In Kruger the species is a year-round resident, with evidence of local movement inside the park rather than a long seasonal migration.

diet.summary: A grazer of short grasses on open plains. When grass is scarce it will also take leaves of shrubs and trees. It drinks often when water is at hand, typically twice a day, and usually stays within reach of a water source.
items: shrub and tree foliage when grass is scarce

young: A single calf is born after a gestation of about 8 to 8.5 months, usually in a short, concentrated season after the rains. Newborns weigh about 19 kg, are tawny brown, and can stand within minutes. They stay close to the cow, and may suckle until the next calf is due. Adult colour starts to appear from about two months. Exact calving months for Kruger were not found in the sources used here.

predators.note: Not a mammal in this guide; listed because it is a documented predator of wildebeest.

habitat: Short-grass plains and open or lightly wooded savanna, usually close to drinking water. It avoids country that is too wet or too arid, and is often seen with zebra on open grassland.

similar.note: Tsessebe lacks the blue wildebeest's black beard, black face and dark brindle stripes on the neck and shoulders. It is a slimmer alcelaphine, and its horns are more lyrate than cow-like.
Lichtenstein's hartebeest has a longer, narrower face and no black beard or brindle shoulder stripes. Its horns rise in a tighter S-curve rather than spreading out in a cow-like parenthesis.

population.notes: SANParks Scientific Services published a 2023 aerial-census range of 16,700–21,948 individuals for blue wildebeest in Kruger (sheet dated March 2025). The official PDF returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) from this environment and was not downloaded or stored. The numeric range is taken from that sheet as reported by visitthekrugerpark.com (read 6 October 2026) and matches the unlabelled 16,700–21,948 (2023) line in a search-index extract of the same PDF. The SANParks Part 2 census blog, which could be fetched, says the 2023 survey found wildebeest among the populations that have increased since the 1990s, but it does not print the numeric range. An earlier SANParks figure cited on the EWT species page is 9,342–17,936 animals in Kruger in 2017, or 12,555 mature individuals; that is kept here as a previous estimate, not as the current one. Regional Red List status is Least Concern.

previousEstimates.notes: Kruger only, cited on the EWT Blue Wildebeest page as SANParks data. The same page also gives 12,555 mature individuals in Kruger in 2017.

upperparts.pattern: dark brown vertical brindle stripes on the neck and the side of the ribcage; back and flanks a little lighter than the underparts

viewNotes.note: A heavy black face, a broad muzzle, and horns that spread out then curve up and in. The black beard hangs below the jaw.
High shoulders sloping to the hips, a stiff black mane, brindle stripes on the neck and shoulder, and a long black tail.
A plain tawny-brown coat, without the adult's black face, beard or brindle stripes. Newborns in the Kruger photographs have not yet grown horns.
Often runs in a loose line or cluster, with the black tail streamed out.

calls.description: A loud nasal grunt or bellow, sometimes written 'ga-noo'. Territorial bulls also snort, and they are the noisiest animals in the rut. A general call of the species is not described as sex-specific in the sources used here, beyond this male territorial calling.

research.note: Text and measurements are sourced, but several size and habit figures come from compiled accounts (Wikipedia, Animal Diversity Web) rather than a southern-African field guide, which was not available. The 2023 Kruger census range could not be read from the official PDF in this session (HTTP 403). Confirm that range against the March 2025 SANParks sheet before treating it as high confidence. Local movement inside Kruger is cited from the EWT species page; a detailed Kruger seasonal map was not found.

gaps: The official SANParks 2023 census PDF (March 2025 sheet) returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) and was not downloaded or stored. The 16,700–21,948 range is cited from a secondary reading of that sheet and a search-index extract, and should be confirmed from the PDF itself.
Macaulay Library search was blocked by a bot-check page, so no licensable recording could be confirmed there.
iNaturalist has 0 sound observations for Connochaetes taurinus in place 69020.
Skinner & Chimimba and Stuart's field guide were not available. Size, diet, habits, young and predators were taken from Wikipedia (citing Kingdon, Huffman, Estes and others) and Animal Diversity Web.
No Kruger-specific calving-month range was found. General accounts give a short calving period after the rains, after a gestation of about 8 to 8.5 months.
Iris colour, ear colour, a sexed shoulder-height split, and underpart colour as a named value were not given in the sources used, so those marks are null.
Live SANParks HTML pages were not used (Phase 1 already recorded HTTP 403; the census PDF was also 403 in this session).
